title: A run's record lives in the plan and in git
description: The gate runner appends every run to an evidence ledger beside the plan, and the readers that grew on it are no longer only a cache of a verdict: the time per task, the repeat of a step whose inputs did not change, the drive's reading of a run it launched in the background, the reading of a red against the base, and the binding of a commit to the run that graded it all read ledger rows. A design that only says the ledger's writes go away would take those with it. So the record moves first, the readers follow through one seam, and the writes stop last, each step with a green gate behind it. The plan and git are the two stores that remain; a row already written stays readable as frozen history and is never migrated. The properties are written before the code: after any number of recorded runs a subject holds exactly one record, the last one printed; a run that exits 0 or 1 has its record in the shard and a record that could not be written is exit 3 naming the log, never exit 0; the pointer is derivable from the record; a decision read from the record equals the run's own output for green and red with no commit made; a recorded run changes no byte inside the content identity; a plan and ledger written by the previous release answer the same after the upgrade, and with the ledger deleted the gate conditions still answer the same. Out of scope here and next in line: the drive's own state, the filed returns, the brief protocol and the subagent writer.
desiredOutcome: A task's verdict is in its commit's Audit-Task, Audit-Gate and Audit-Run trailers, the newest run of every task and phase is one record in its own shard, a phase's CI run is in its shard, every reader of recorded runs goes through one reader over those records and the frozen older rows, the base is measured only when a red could predate the task, and no evidence row, per-call journal row or preimage file is written under the default configuration.

findings.issue: The seven install steps are written out twice, and the only thing holding them together is a comment ('a change to one is owed to the other', ci.yml:~356). Nothing compares them, so a later edit to one job (a package-name tweak, a key change) leaves the other on the old shell with every gate green. The task's own dependants named gate-parity.py's matrix rules; none covers this.
findings.resolution: Move the steps into a composite action (.github/actions/browser-install/action.yml) that both jobs call, or add a gate-parity rule that fails when the two jobs' install step lists differ. Either replaces the prose rule with a mechanism.

findings.issue: The step title 'the archive is asked only for a .deb the restored set lacks' and the log line 'not in the restored set, so fetched from the archive: $fetch' say the archive is asked for the missing .deb. The code passes $MISSING, not $fetch, to apt-get install --download-only, and apt sees only the fresh $dl directory, so on a partial set the archive is asked for the whole set plus its dependency closure and cp overwrites the restored files. The result is correct (that .deb is fetched), but the claim is narrower than the behaviour and only the miss path was exercised on a real runner. Separately, the ls check names only the packages in $MISSING, so a restored set missing a dependency-only .deb (a package apt pulled in that playwright did not name) is not detected and dpkg -i fails with an unmet dependency: a red job, not a green one.
findings.resolution: Either reword the title and log line to say the whole set is refetched when any one is absent, or install $fetch and let the dependency closure follow. Optionally verify the restored set with `dpkg-deb --info` per file, or by `dpkg -i` failing over into one refetch.

findings.issue: A poisoned or truncated cache entry is permanent. Cache keys are immutable and an exact hit is never re-saved, so a bad .deb in a saved entry makes dpkg -i fail (red) on every run of that branch until the key changes or GitHub evicts it, and the step has no path that drops a restored set it cannot install. The same holds for the partial set in finding 2: the repair is not persisted, so each later run repeats the full fetch. The entry can only come to hold a bad file if the job that saved it was green, so this is unlikely, and every outcome seen in the shell is red, not a green job without the packages. The sysdeps key also omits runner.arch, which the browser key carries; a .deb for another architecture would be refused by dpkg (red).
findings.resolution: Add a manual version token to the sysdeps key (chromium-sysdeps-v1-...) so a poisoned entry can be bypassed without a code change, include runner.arch in it, and on a dpkg -i failure fall back once to the fetch path before failing.

findings.issue: The descriptive line says 'The browser jobs' install drops from 3-9 minutes to 12-26 seconds'. The before figures are slow-mirror runs; the after figures come from two fast-mirror runs, and the pre-change install on a fast mirror was 38s (run 41322244766). The change's measured saving is the 21s to 12s (panel) and 26s to 15s (report) between the miss and hit runs, and a miss on a slow mirror costs what it cost before, minus the upgrades. The ci.yml comments say exactly this; the outcome summary does not. Also, main's push runs skip the browser jobs, so main saves no entry and the first run on a new ci/ branch misses both caches, so the hit path may be the rarer one in this repo's own practice; nothing here measures the hit rate.
findings.resolution: State in the outcome that the measured install is 12-26s on a fast mirror on both paths and that the slow-mirror saving is a hit-only saving not measured; decide separately whether a workflow_dispatch on main should seed the caches.

findings.issue: The new behaviour, a verified push to main running the browser jobs with seed true, was executed by no real run. All four logs read 'seed: false' and show seen-browser and seen-sysdeps as outcome=skipped (run2-browserpanel lines 250-253); the plan step took its 'SEED != true' early exit. So actions/cache/restore@v6 with lookup-only, the cache-hit output read by the plan step, the 'entry exists for both keys, nothing installed' branch, the 'one key missing' branch and the workflow's `seed: needs.verified.outputs.run != ''` wiring have been shown only on the uncommitted stub harness. The task's acceptance 1 asked for 'a run on the default-branch path that saves the entries'; the probes were workflow_dispatch runs on a ci/ branch, which exercise the install and the save but not the seed decision. The first real execution of the seed path will be a push to main.
findings.resolution: Before landing, push one more probe commit to a ci/ branch with `seed: true` hard-wired and the slice step skipped, and read two runs: the first must print 'seed: no entry exists for the browser key and the system packages' key' then save; the second must print 'seed: an entry exists for every key this image needs, so nothing is installed and nothing is saved' and show every later step skipped. Add a third look at a run with only one of the two keys present if a cheap way exists (a changed BROWSER_CACHE_VERSION on one key is not possible, so state that this half stays stub-only).

findings.issue: Nothing in the repository guards the action's shell besides a real CI run. I searched tracked files: no test, lint or checker names .github/actions or action.yml (git grep for 'action.yml|.github/actions|actionlint|shellcheck' over tools/tests/.claude/plugins finds nothing), gate-parity.py reads only ci.yml, and the 20-case stub harness the proofs rest on (scratchpad stubs/harness.py) is not committed. The first real run found three defects the stubs could not see (Permission denied from cp -a, the image version in the key, jc0). The failure shape is also quiet: any bug that makes the hit path throw lands in `why`, the fallback fetches from the archive, and the job stays GREEN with one ::warning:: and a cache that never helps. No gate reads that warning, so the regression the whole task exists to remove (a first run paying the archive) can return with every check green. A later change (apt flags, BROWSER_CACHE_VERSION, a new package) has only a 13-minute hosted run as feedback and nothing that notices a hit turning into a fallback.
findings.resolution: Commit the harness as tests/test_browser_install.py with the `N/M cases passed` contract: extract the `run:` bodies from action.yml by step id, run them under the stub PATH, and keep si1-si10 and the sk/sp cases (full hit asks nothing, miss, partial, dependency missing, unreadable .deb falls back once, fallback failing is red). Add one case that fails when the hit path prints the ::warning:: (the hit must not fall back). If a suite is out of scope for this task, file it as the next task and name it in the outcome; the claim that the install is guarded cannot rest on an uncommitted harness.

findings.issue: An untouched sentence this diff makes false, which the return's claim 3 dismisses as 'pre-existing inexactness about verified unchanged by this task'. PLUGIN-BUILD-GUIDE.md:7699 reads 'a push to main whose commit a run already verified runs only tools/ci-verified.py'. Before this change that was exact (every other job was skipped by `needs.verified.outputs.run == ''`); after it the two browser jobs run their checkout, setup, npm ci, lookups and install on that push. The task named 'the push-to-default-branch path that skips work for a verified commit' as a dependant to answer for by name, and this document is the one that describes that path outside CONTRIBUTING.md.
findings.resolution: Change the sentence to say that such a push runs `verified` and, in the two browser jobs, the install only (seeding the caches), and correct claim 3 so it lists this line as made false by the task rather than left. The same pass should re-read tools/check-rendered-artifacts.py:1429, tools/lints/_refs.py:1915 and CLAUDE.md:314 ('every job is setup plus one verify.sh call'), which stay inexact only about `verified` and are unchanged by this diff.

findings.issue: On a push to main whose commit is verified, the browser jobs now do work that can fail: npm ci and `playwright install-deps --dry-run` run before the seed decision even when both entries exist (they are needed only to name the keys), and a miss runs apt and the Chromium download. A transient npm, apt or network failure turns that main run red for a cache it did not need. That is the failure class the `verified` job exists to remove (its own comment: re-running the same bytes 'could only add a ... intermittent the first draw did not have'). It does not skip any slice, and no gate reads main's run, so the cost is a red check on an already-verified commit, not a lost verdict.
findings.resolution: Give the two jobs `continue-on-error: ${{ needs.verified.outputs.run != '' }}` so a failed seed is visible but not red, or compute the playwright pin and image name without npm ci on the seed path. Say in ci.yml which is chosen.

findings.issue: On main a running run is never cancelled and one pending run is held; a third push replaces the pending one, which then never runs. A verified push used to finish in about half a minute; it now holds the group for the seed's duration (a hit: checkout, node, npm ci, two lookups; a miss: the full install, 2m20s on the measured fast-mirror miss and up to the install's 9m22s fetch on a slow day). A commit queued behind a seeding miss is more likely to be replaced and get no run on main.
findings.resolution: State it in the comment above browser-panel as a cost of seeding, or have the seed job take its own concurrency group (`concurrency: browser-seed`) so it does not hold ci-refs/heads/main.

findings.issue: Two statements go past what the logs show. (a) outcome.descriptive says 'a hit asks the archive for nothing on any image version of the distribution'; one cross-image restore was measured (set saved on 20261111.127.1, restored on 20261111.370.1) and the action's own header (action.yml:27-44) says an image whose installed versions the set's index cannot satisfy falls back to a fresh fetch and keeps doing so on every run. (b) outcome.technical attributes the report job's 35s after the restore to 'apt Reading package lists 18s plus dpkg Reading database about 10s'. In run2-browserreport the 'Reading package lists...' line is 20:12:41.008 and the dependency listing follows at 20:12:41.34; the 18.5s gap is between 'The following NEW packages will be installed' (20:12:41.348) and '0 upgraded, 9 newly installed' (20:12:59.923), which is not apt's index read. The panel job's same stretch took 2.6s (20:12:30.0 to 20:12:32.6), so the gap is variable and unexplained, not shown to be local.
findings.resolution: Write (a) as 'on the image versions measured' and (b) as 'an unexplained 18s between the dependency listing and the summary line, not seen in the panel job'. The committed comments already avoid both claims; only the return's wording needs the change.

findings.issue: contradicts task clause "the recorder takes the phase lock with a bounded wait behind any verb's write" and acceptance 4 ("a verb's write and a background record write, interleaved in both orders, both land"). write_record takes `phase-<id>`, but every audit-task.py verb reads and writes the shard under the INDEX lock (`_under_lock` -> `_panel_write.acquire_index_lock`, LOCK_NAME "index" at _panel_write.py:392); the only `phase-<id>` holders are `start`'s claim and the drive's phase run. So a verb's read-modify-write and the recorder's are not mutually exclusive. Probe in a scratch copy: index lock held by a stand-in verb, write_record returned written=True after 0.02s without waiting, then the verb's write from its earlier read left the shard with neither lastRun nor testEvidence (and the reverse order loses the verb's write, e.g. a `done`). lr4 passes only because its stand-in verb takes `phase-P1`, which no real verb does; lr5 ("the other order") asserts only what the test's own read-modify-write does and goes red only when lr4's landing is missing (M1 and M2 each reddened it as a knock-on). CHANGELOG, manifest-conventions.md and PLUGIN-BUILD-GUIDE.md repeat the claim ("so neither write loses the other's key"). The old pointer write had the same exposure; what is new is the claim, and that the shard now holds the only copy of the record and of the stages.
findings.resolution: Make the recorder's write exclude the verbs: take the index lock as well as the phase lock (one fixed order, checked against `start`, which takes `phase-<id>` while a verb holds the index lock), or have the verbs' shard writes take the phase lock. Re-aim lr4 so the stand-in verb takes the lock real verbs take (drive a real `audit-task.py note` against the same project), and either give lr5 a product assertion or drop it. Until then, correct the three documents so they promise what is true: a wait behind `phase-<id>` holders only.

findings.issue: The repeated-verdict arm has no case, and it fails silent. Deleting the copy (`steps = []` for the `source` branch) left test__evidence_io 361/361 and test_run_test_gate 699/699 green (M6, both suites run in a scratch copy): every lr case runs with `--no-reuse`, and no case passes `source=` to run_record. The clause "a copied step carries its source's verdict fields forward, so ... no older record is needed to read it" is therefore shown by nothing. The source is read only from the ledger row (`row_by_run`); when that row is not there - the day the later task stops writing rows, or a rotated ledger - the record is `steps: []` with `verdictSource: reused` and no marker that its steps are unavailable (probe: run_record(reused_row, source=None) -> steps []). Separately, the record keeps the read-back's own startedAt and durationMs (probe: durationMs 120, startedAt of the repeat) while the schema says startedAt is "absent on a run that repeated another's verdict, which measured nothing", and nothing on the record separates those figures from a measurement except `verdictSource`.
findings.resolution: Add a gate-level case (reuse on, second run) and a run_record(source=...) case asserting the copied steps, their per-step reusedFrom and the absence of per-step durationMs; take the source from the subject's previous `lastRun` when the ledger row is gone, and say `stepsUnavailable` (or equivalent) when neither is there rather than writing an empty list. For a repeated run either omit startedAt/durationMs/selectionMs from the record or state in the schema that they are the read-back's own.

findings.issue: Two writers of one key can leave `testEvidence` naming a run other than `lastRun`, against the doc's "the two always name one run" and COMPATIBILITY's "runId, status and at in it are the values testEvidence caches". reconcile takes the ledger row when it is stamped after the record (the run whose record write was refused, exit 3) and calls write_pointer, which moves only the pointer; lastRun keeps the older run. Also write_pointer still reads the shard BEFORE it takes the lock (read_json at 2542, acquire at 2553, save at 2567), so a reconcile racing a recorder saves its stale body over the recorder's lastRun and timing stages. The task's clause says reconcile does to lastRun what it does to testEvidence.
findings.resolution: In reconcile, when the ledger row wins, also write `run_record(row)` so the pair stays one run, or soften the two sentences to "names one run except after a refused record write, until the next recorded run". Read the shard under the lock in write_pointer, as write_record now does (share `_holders`).

findings.issue: Stale text contradicts the new behaviour: the `--record` help reads "a green run whose row could not be stored exits 3 (0 passed, 1 failed, 2 usage, 3 passed but unrecorded)" and the E_UNRECORDED comment says "the gate is green and the record the caller asked for does not exist"; a red run now exits 3 as well (lr6), and `unrecorded_line` says so. A pre-push or CI step reading `--help` is told that 1 is always the work's failure.
findings.resolution: Reword both to "a run (green or red) whose row or whose record in the plan could not be stored exits 3".

findings.issue: A stale phase lock is refused at once, with no wait (probe: dead holder, wait=5, returned in 0.00s), so every recorded gate of that phase exits 3 until a human runs `audit-lock --takeover`; that is the designed rule, but the sentence it prints is garbled by the hint: "...use audit-lock --takeover, then nothing was written to the plan". It names no repair, and the gate's own closing line says "re-run once the phase lock is free" for a run that may have taken minutes.
findings.resolution: Pass a hint that names the repair ("then re-run this gate; nothing was written to the plan") so both the stale and the held sentences read, and say in `unrecorded_line` that the ledger row stands, so `--reconcile` is not mistaken for the repair of a missing record.

findings.issue: The drive finds the run it launched by a launch token that exists only on the plan's record; the ledger row never carries it, and the union adds it to a row only while the record still holds that same run. When another run of the same subject is recorded after the launched one (a hand-run /audit:run, a sibling session, /audit:review during a background phase gate), or the launched run's record write was refused on the lock, run_by_launch returns None for good and the drive keeps answering wait-gate with 'no gate row ... since', which is false: the ledger holds the row. The code this replaced found it. Established by reading and a function-level probe (a ledger row without a token plus a newer record carrying another token gives None); case lt2 covers only the other order.
findings.resolution: Put the launch token on the ledger row as well (an identity key of the row), and when the subject's newest run is later than the launch and carries another token, say the launched run was replaced and by which run instead of waiting.

findings.issue: A record still lacks fields readers of the one seam take from a row, so a run held only as a record gives them None or an empty list with nothing saying so: followersOwed (the drive's run_followers returns [], and a red that owes regenerated followers is decided as a plain red), gateReach and its not-asked twin (a repeated verdict prints that the source run recorded no reach reading, which is false), observations, treeMutated and coverage (the panel and the report would say no comparison was made). Masked today because ledger rows are still written. Established by a probe: run_record of a row carrying these kept only at, runId and steps.
findings.resolution: Derive the record's keys from what the readers of the seam read rather than from a hand list: carry these fields, and hold the list to the readers with a case that fails when a reader takes a row key the record does not carry.

findings.issue: Several callers of read_rows pass no manifest path, so the records they read are those of the plan the project's config names, while write_record writes to the plan the command was handed. For a command run against another plan in the same project (the examples' plans; task ids such as P1.1 collide), reuse and the lookup of a repeat's source read a foreign plan's records: the repeat's source is not found, or another plan's record is read as this plan's subject. Established by reading; the drive is not affected (its config comes from project_config_for).
findings.resolution: Every caller hands the seam the plan it was handed; make the plan a required argument of the seam so a caller that forgets it is an error rather than a silent default.

findings.issue: The importer refuses a whole ledger file when any of its runs is held as a record in the plan. For a project whose plan travels with git and whose evidence files do not, a run recorded on another machine arrives in the committed shard first, and importing that machine's ledger file is then refused with 'already in <plan file>', losing every other row of the file and the fuller row of that run. The stated reason (a run counted twice) does not apply: the union keeps one entry per run id and the ledger row wins.
findings.resolution: Only a run held as a ledger row is a duplicate; a run held only as a record is imported, and the union's own rule decides which copy a reader sees. Cases for both.

findings.issue: Messages still name the ledger alone or print a figure nobody counted: '--base-of' says no run is recorded in the ledger, the drive says the evidence ledger holds no row, the panel's dangling sentence prints '0 files read' and never reads ledgerAbsent (the task's fifth acceptance point), and the binding says no gate verdict is recorded when the subject's shard could not be read.
findings.resolution: Each message names both places it looked, and an unreadable shard is said as unreadable with the file.

findings.issue: Plan files that will not read go unreported in three places (close-phase skips an unreadable shard at the tip silently and gives no note when the tip is unreadable but a worktree exists; the importer ignores unreadablePlanFiles), and there are three walkers of a plan's shards with three error rules (plan_bodies, subject_records, close-phase's tip_bodies).
findings.resolution: One walker with one rule for a shard that will not read, used by all three, which reports the file.

findings.issue: Two sentences of the Tests section are no longer exact once the browser jobs carry an install step that a seed run may fail and a warning step: 'every CI job is setup plus one tools/verify.sh --only <slices> call' (already inexact for the verified job), and the enumeration of what gate-parity.py checks lacks the rule that a step or job running a slice is never allowed to fail. Reported by the executor of the cache task; CLAUDE.md is the project's instruction file and is not edited on an agent's report.
findings.resolution: The owner decides the wording; the paragraph already points at gate-parity's docstring as the current statement, so the repair may be to delete the enumeration and keep the pointer.

findings.issue: The new mask replaces ` *\b<duration>` with a fixed ` <duration>`, so it swallows the whole run of spaces between the exit code and the duration as well as the digit-dependent padding. A change to the step line's column layout that only a present-but-empty executor.phaseGateOnly caused (the gap between `exit N` and the duration) is no longer visible to pgo7. Measured in a scratch copy: a runner that, only when the key is present, widens that gap (`exit 0  ` -> `exit 0     `) is FAIL under the old mask and PASS under the new one. The class pgo7 exists for (the setting changing what the runner prints) is still caught for an extra line, a reworded banner, a renamed step, a changed check-count text and a changed duration unit; only pure whitespace layout inside the swallowed gap is lost.
findings.resolution: Keep the layout invariant instead of dropping it: the width of (padding + duration text) is constant for one exit-code width, so substitute with a function that returns `"<duration>".rjust(len(match.group(0)))` (or equivalent) rather than a fixed ' <duration>'. The digit-count-dependent padding then still collapses to one spelling while a real column-width change still reddens the case.

tasks.title: The browser jobs' time bound is about the slice: the Chromium install is timed by step and cached, and each bound's basis is re-measured
tasks.description:
The `browser (report)` job is bounded at 19 minutes on a recorded longest run of about nine, and on three runs in one day it took 17m44s once and was cut at the bound twice, the second time with the slice's VERIFY OK printed in the same second. Two costs sit in that job and in `browser (panel)` beside it. The install step (`npm ci`, then `npx playwright install --with-deps chromium`) took between six and nine minutes. The slice took over eleven where its recorded longest whole job was nine.

Measure before changing: split the install into steps that each print their own duration (the package install, the browser download, the system packages) and read one run. Then remove what can be removed: cache the browser download keyed by the pinned playwright version in the lock file, and install only the system packages the runner image lacks. A cache miss must still install and pass; a cache hit must not skip a version change. For the slice: read its per-step seconds from the run's log (verify.sh prints them) and compare with the run the `longest` line names; if a step grew, name it and the commit range in the outcome and file what you find rather than fixing a product regression inside this task.

Then re-record: each browser job's `longest` line names a run measured after this change, and its bound is two to three times that, which is the rule tools/gate-parity.py holds. Do not raise a bound to make room for a cost you did not measure.

ACCEPTANCE.
1. One dispatched run (the orchestrator dispatches it on the phase's CI branch; say in the outcome which lines to read) shows the install by step, and a second shows the cached path with its seconds.
2. `python3 tools/gate-parity.py` is green: every job's bound is backed by its `longest` line.
3. The outcome states the job's whole duration before and after, each with its run id, and what remains of the slice's growth.
4. Nothing in the slice itself is skipped, narrowed or moved to the release tier to buy time.

DEPENDANTS to answer for by name: tools/gate-parity.py's job bounds and its matrix rules, tools/verify.sh's slices (unchanged), CONTRIBUTING.md and CLAUDE.md where they describe CI's shape, and the release-tier jobs that share the install step.

outcome.technical: Only .github/workflows/ci.yml changed. (1) The single `npm ci && npx playwright install --with-deps chromium` step in browser (panel) and browser (report) is now seven steps, identical in both jobs: npm ci; read the playwright-core pin from package-lock.json and ImageOS/ImageVersion (exits 1 if any is missing); actions/cache@v6 on <home>/.cache/ms-playwright keyed by runner os/arch and the playwright-core version; `npx playwright install chromium`, run on a hit as well so a version change is never skipped; derive the packages `playwright install-deps --dry-run chromium` names that dpkg-query does not report installed (exits 1 if no install line or no package); actions/cache@v6 on <home>/.cache/chromium-sysdeps keyed by the image version and a hash of that list; then `apt-get update` plus `--download-only` only for a .deb the restored set lacks, followed by `dpkg -i` on the set. Only the packages the image lacks are named, so mesa is no longer upgraded. (2) Measured on head 55d48673. Run 44363694425 missed both caches: panel 17:53:48-17:59:19 = 5m31s, report 17:53:48-18:05:59 = 12m11s, install 21s and 26s, mirror fast ('Fetched 21.1 MB in 0s'/'in 1s'). Run 44366022835 hit both ('every package the image lacks is in the restored set; no archive is asked'): panel 18:06:27-18:12:04 = 5m37s, report 18:06:27-18:19:04 = 12m37s, install 12s and 15s. Before the change: report 17m44s (run 44341247041) and 17m57s (run 44270291891); runs 44318839994 and 44356971266 were cut at the bound; panel 11m36s (44341247041) and 14m49s (42283005055); install 3m25s to 9m05s in the four runs read today, nearly all of it the apt fetch (for example 32.1 MB in 8m11s at 65.4 kB/s, job 134852070227). (3) The `longest` lines now read browser-panel 5m37s and browser-report 12m37s (both run 44366022835, start and end given), and the PROVISIONAL marking is gone. The bounds are 16 (panel; allowed 11m14s-16m51s, set above the minimum to hold a slow miss) and 26 (report; minimum 25m14s). A comment says what a slow miss still costs: the fetch of the packages the image lacks, 19.1 MB in 9m22s at 34.0 kB/s in run 42283005055, about nine minutes added to either job. The two measured runs had a fast mirror, so they show no saving on a slow day; the comment says so. (4) The slice is unchanged and still the remaining pole. The report slice took 11m25s (miss) and 12m04s (hit), against 8m13s in run 41322244766, the run the old `longest` line named (its log is still readable). Growth there: interactive-check steps 1m00s -> 3m00s, one-status 47s -> 2m18s, live plan 6m18s -> 5m47s; checks per page about tripled (acme-store 200 -> 584). Source: tools/check-report-interactive.mjs, commits 03f4114d (P163.1) through 1d0e3673 (P165.5). Filed in the fault register by the orchestrator, not fixed here. The report job is now about 12.5 minutes against the ten-minute workflow budget; the panel is about 5.5. (5) The cache helps only within one branch, or across branches when main holds a saved entry. Main's push runs skip the browser jobs once a commit is verified, so main rarely saves one; seeding it is the owner's call. (6) Process note: in stage two three Edit calls were refused with 'File has not been read yet' (file state was lost on resume). tasks.description:
The commit verb writes the verdict it bound the commit to into the commit itself. Today a task commit carries Audit-Row (a journal nonce) and an optional Co-Authored-By; which run graded it is known only through the evidence ledger and the journal. Add: Audit-Task: <task id>; Audit-Gate: <status> <gate digest>; Audit-Run: <runId>; and, when the verb was told to commit over a verdict, Audit-Override: <the reason, verbatim>. The values come from the one place that already decides them, the verdict binding the verb asks before it commits (_verdict_binding.binding): the trailers name the run the binding bound, never another, so a commit made in the phase tree after a wave member's bytes were integrated names the run that graded the phase tree's bytes. Audit-Row stays as it is.

Reading: _commit_trail.py gains the reader, over git log alone. A commit carrying Audit-Task and no Audit-Gate reads as no verdict recorded, never as passed. A commit carrying no Audit-Task (every commit made before this release, and every commit made by hand) is not a trailer commit and its verdict is read as before. Status (_status_facts.py) and the report (_evidence_view.py) read a done task's verdict at its commit from the trailers, and say which source they read.

6. A commit made over a tree other than the one the bound run graded is refused as today; the new trailers do not weaken that refusal.

tasks.title: The newest run of a task or a phase is one record in its own shard, written by the gate under the phase lock
tasks.description:
Add the record that will replace the ledger row, beside the row, changing no reader yet. After a recorded run (run-test-gate.py --record, task or phase scope) the subject in its shard carries `lastRun`: the run's id, moments and durations (startedAt, durationMs, selectionMs), status and failed list, verdictSource and reusedFrom, the reuse key, the gate digest and source, leftToPhaseGate, the tested state (head, dirty, tree key), the banners and the machine and attribution lines, and per step: name, exit, ran, outcome, failing lines up to the existing cap, the measured duration when measured here, and reusedFrom when copied. A copied step carries its source's verdict fields forward, so the record is the newest measurement of each current step and no older record is needed to read it. `testEvidence` stays the three-key pointer and is written from the record in the same write. Replace, never append.

The write. Today the pointer write is skipped when the phase lock is held, because the ledger row stands anyway. A record that is the only copy cannot be skipped: the recorder takes the phase lock with a bounded wait behind any verb's write, and a record it still could not write is exit 3 naming the log path. Never exit 0 or 1 without the record. A verb that rewrites a task (move, reopen, group sign-off's copy of a carrier's pointer, reconcile) does to `lastRun` what it does to `testEvidence`.

The launch. `--launch <token>` is stored on the record, so a caller that started the run in the background can find the record of exactly that run.

Time. The recorder appends the gate and the selection stage to the task's `timing` itself, in the same locked write, from the same figures, citing the run by id; today the drive queues them in its own state from the ledger row. The stage survives the record's replacement.

ACCEPTANCE (each a case).
1. After five recorded runs of one gate a subject holds exactly one `lastRun`, its runId is the last one printed, and the shard is no larger than after the first run.
2. Exit 0 or 1 implies the shard's record names the printed runId and status; a lock that stays held past the wait is exit 3 naming the log, and the shard is unchanged.
3. `testEvidence` equals the pointer derived from `lastRun`; delete the pointer and reconcile restores it from the record.
4. A verb's write and a background record write, interleaved in both orders, both land: neither field is lost.
5. A recorded run changes no byte inside the content identity: the reuse key is the same before and after, and the set of paths the run modified (git status in a fixture) is exactly what recorded_paths names.
6. The record's size is bounded by the gate's width: failing lines per step at the existing cap, steps no more than declared plus derived. Print the measured bytes for this repository's own task gate in the outcome.
7. The schema accepts `lastRun` on a task and on a phase, a plan without it validates unchanged, and a one-file plan and a per-phase plan both carry it.
8. A machine path in a failing line reads scrubbed, as every string the shard write passes does, and the verdict fields are untouched.
9. The evidence row is still written, byte for byte as before, with the same runId as the record.

tasks.description:
`_evidence_io.read_rows` is the seam every reader of recorded runs already goes through (count its callers with grep before you start and put the count's command in the outcome). Make what it returns the union of the frozen ledger rows and the `lastRun` records of the plan's subjects, each record presented in the row's shape, one entry per runId (a run present as both is one entry). Then prove that nothing downstream needs the ledger: for a fixture holding records only and the same fixture holding rows only, each of these gives the same answer - the verdict binding (_verdict_binding.binding, with its reused row followed to the measured source), the step repeat (reusable_run, repeated_step_sources, step_parts) and its part-reused result, the reading of a red against the base (base_run), latest_by_subject, row_by_run, the gate's mean, the drive's read-back of a run it launched (green and red, with no commit made, and a red read back runs no step), close-phase's reading of a branch's runs (it reads the branch's ledger texts through git today; it must read the branch's shards the same way), and audit-task's --failing-from and couple --basis-run (resolve against records and rows, or refuse naming both places).

The drive finds the record of the run it launched by the launch token, not by comparing the subject's run ids against a list kept in its own state.

With one record per subject, a rule written over 'the newest row for the identity' has only one candidate; where a branch can no longer be reached (a newer row for the same identity), delete it and its case rather than leaving it unreachable, and name each deleted branch in the outcome.

1. The table: every reader named above, records-only against rows-only, same answer.
2. A second ask on an unchanged tree, with records only, measures exactly the steps the left-out reading names and copies every other, each copy naming a run that measured it.
3. A record whose reuse key is not the current key repeats nothing.
4. The drive's decision read from the record equals the run's own --json for green and for red, with no commit made; reading a red back runs no gate step.
5. A reader of history that finds no older directory says so with a basis; it never prints a zero as if it had counted.
6. A plan and ledger as the previous release wrote them (use a committed example or build the fixture from real rows) give the same status, report and gate-condition answers before and after this change.

tasks.title: The base is measured only when a red could predate the task, its verdict is kept per commit, and the writer is not held for it
tasks.description:
After a red task gate the drive measures the phase's base so that a red the base already has is not blamed on the task. Today that measurement is due whenever the reading is no-base or not-knowable, the red's decision is held until the base verdict exists, and the verdict lives in a base-scope ledger row, a progress record under the drive's state and a mark. State the rule as a property of the records and move the verdict where it survives.

Needed means all three: the task gate is red; some failing case or step is not one a file this task's `tests.add` created (a case the task itself added cannot predate it); and no clean-tree measurement of that step at that base commit is recorded. Otherwise no base run is started and the decision says which of the three made it unnecessary.

Kept means: the base verdict for a commit is in the plan (on the red task's record, keyed by the base commit, readable through the one reader), computed at most once per commit and step set, and a second red at the same base reads it.

Not held means: when a writer session exists to resume, the red's failing lines go to it at once, and the base runs beside it; if the base then shows the same red, the next decision says so and the writer is not resumed over it again. Where no session exists (the dispatched writer), the decision is offered with the base named as still running rather than withheld.

Keep what the phase before this one fixed: one liveness reading decides both the reading of a base run's record and the removal of its tree.

ACCEPTANCE.
1. A red whose failing cases all live in files the task's tests.add created starts no base run, and the decision says why.
2. A second red at the same base commit and step set starts no base run and reads the kept verdict, which equals the first.
3. A red with a session to resume sends the failing lines before the base verdict exists; a base that then shows the same red produces the base decision and no further resume over that red.
4. A base run killed mid-way leaves no tree and no claim behind after the next call, as today.
5. The seconds: print, for one red on this repository's own plan, the wall time from the red to the writer's resume before and after, measured twice with a gap.

tasks.title: A case that compares two gate runs' printed lines says which line differed, and its Windows-only red has a named cause
tasks.description:
One case of tests/test_run_test_gate.py, pgo7, failed once on a Windows CI runner (run 44363694425, job "selftests (windows, plain 2)") over product code that passed it on the same runner image in two other runs the same day. The case runs a task's gate once with executor.phaseGateOnly absent and once with it empty and asserts that the two print the same lines once ids and times are masked. In the failing run both exited 0 with the same steps and the same row keys, so the difference is in the printed lines, and the failure message does not show them. A case that reddens a green tree once in three runs is how a CI verdict stops being read.

Do this in order. First, make the case's failure say what differed: when the masked line lists are unequal, the message carries the first differing pair of lines (and the lengths if they differ), so the next red of this case names its own cause. Second, read the failing job's log (gh run view --job with the job's id from that run, read-only) for anything the run printed around the case, and read the case's mask against every line the gate prints: a duration that changes unit between two runs (ms to s), a count of workers or slots, a path under a temp directory with a random part, a line that appears only when a step crosses a time threshold, the order of two lines written by different streams. Third, fix the cause where it is: if a line legitimately varies with time, the mask must cover its whole varying part; if a line appears or not depending on timing, the two runs are not comparable on that line and the case must say so rather than compare it; if the product prints something nondeterministic that a user would also see vary, that is a product fix and belongs in run-test-gate.py.

ACCEPTANCE.
1. With the two line lists made to differ in one line (a mutation in a scratch copy, restored in the same command), the failure message names that line pair.
2. The cause is named in the outcome with the evidence that it is the cause (the log line, or the unmasked form found by reading), or stated as not established with what was ruled out; a mask widened without a named cause is not accepted.
3. The case still fails when executor.phaseGateOnly set to an empty list changes what a task's run prints: prove it by mutation.
4. The suite is green under the sweep and under the cp1252 leg locally (python3 tools/sweep-selftests.py tests/test_run_test_gate.py, and the same with --encoding cp1252).

DEPENDANTS: the suite's other cases that share pgo7's masking helper, if it is shared.

(2) CAUSE, reproduced: the step line is '  %-12s exit %-3d %10s  %s' (run-test-gate.py:5047), so the duration is right-aligned in a 10-wide column. _pgo_masked collapsed each digit run to N but kept the padding, which still encodes the digit count. A step at 111 ms in one fixture and 73 ms in the other masks to '      N ms' against '       N ms'. Raw diff seen locally under load: 'sweep exit 0       111 ms' / 'sweep exit 0        73 ms'. Unloaded, steps here take about 30 ms and never cross 100 ms, so the case passes; on CI, trivial steps sit near 100 ms (pr3 in the failing Windows run 44363694425 printed row=156 for a row of one trivial measured step). pgo7 was red in 44363694425 (windows plain 2), 44366022835 and 44388480667 (linux stress 1). (3) FIX in the mask, not the product: the duration field (the spaces before it, the number and the unit, in every form _fmt.human_duration renders, _fmt.py:187-193: N ms, N.N s, N m NN s) becomes one ' <duration>' token, applied before the digit collapse. The column is intended product behaviour (run-test-gate.py:5039-5045 states why it is right-aligned), so no product change is owed. A check over 13 durations from 0 ms to one hour gave a single masked line. The first attempt at (a) and (b) keyed on the parsed names and SURVIVED, because phase_gate_only_setting returns ((), None) for absent and for empty alike (_config_rules.py:319-328), so it fired in both arms. tasks.title: A branch's first CI run restores the browser install: the default branch seeds the cache, the install is written once, a partial set fetches what it names and a bad entry heals
tasks.description:
The browser jobs now restore the Chromium download and the system packages the runner image lacks from a cache, and the first measurement shows what that buys and what it does not. A cache entry is saved only by a job that succeeded, and an entry is readable by the branch that saved it and by branches cut from the default branch's entries. The default branch's push runs skip the browser jobs when the commit is already verified, so the default branch saves no entry, and every phase's CI branch misses both caches on its first run. On a miss the archive is asked for about as many megabytes as before the change (the package index plus the font packages), so on a day the runner's mirror is slow the first run of a branch still pays minutes; the two runs measured so far had a fast mirror and differ by seconds. The review of that change also found three things in its shell.

Make a hit the ordinary case, and make the steps do what their names say:
1. Seed. The default branch holds a saved entry for both keys after any push that changes a key's inputs (the playwright pin in the lock file, the runner image version, the list of packages the image lacks), so a branch's first run restores it. Do it with the least new machinery that is honest: a job that runs only the install steps and saves the caches, on the default branch, when no entry for the key exists. It carries a time bound and a `longest` line like every job, and tools/gate-parity.py's rules must hold it (a job outside the slices: say how the parity rules read it, and extend them if they cannot).
2. One install, written once. The two browser jobs and the seeding job run the same steps; today the block is written out twice with a comment asking that both be changed together. Put it in one place the three jobs call (a composite action under .github/actions/ is the established form), or hold the copies to one text with a gate-parity rule that names a difference. A prose rule is not enough.
3. A partial set fetches what it names. When some but not all packages are in the restored set, the step downloads the missing ones and their dependencies and nothing else, and the check that decides a package is present covers the dependencies the install needs, not only the packages named. The step's title and log line say what the code does.
4. A bad entry heals. The system-packages key carries the runner's architecture as the browser key does. When installing from a restored set fails, the step falls back once to fetching from the archive and says so; a job is red only when that also fails. A manual version token in the key lets an operator retire an entry.

ACCEPTANCE.
1. The orchestrator dispatches runs for you as before (hand back READY-FOR-RUN with what to read, do not file): a run on the default-branch path that saves the entries, and a first run of a fresh branch that restores both. State what each line of each log must show.
2. Proven on stubs in your outcome, as the first change was: a full hit, a miss, a partial set (one package missing, one dependency missing), a restored set with a truncated package (the fallback runs once and the step passes), and the fallback failing (the step is red).
3. `python3 tools/gate-parity.py` is green and each job's bound is backed by its `longest` line; the seeding job's line names a measured run.
4. No slice is skipped, narrowed or moved; the release tier's jobs are unchanged.
5. The outcome says what a branch's first run costs after the change on a slow mirror, with the basis, and what it cost before.

DEPENDANTS to answer for by name: tools/gate-parity.py's job-bound, slice and matrix rules, tools/verify.sh's slices (unchanged), CONTRIBUTING.md and CLAUDE.md where they describe CI's shape (CLAUDE.md is outside this task's files: say what sentence there, if any, is no longer exact), and the push-to-default-branch path that skips work for a verified commit.

outcome.technical: WHAT CHANGED. (1) .github/actions/browser-install/action.yml (new composite action) holds the install once; browser-panel and browser-report call it, and the two inline copies are deleted from ci.yml. Its steps: npm ci; pins (playwright-core pin, ImageOS, arch, BROWSER_CACHE_VERSION=1; the image version is logged, not keyed); naming the packages the image lacks; seed-only lookups (actions/cache/restore lookup-only) and a decide step; restore and install of the browser; restore of the system packages' set (debs/ plus lists/, the apt index they were resolved against); and the install step. The install step asks apt `--print-uris` against the set's own index what the install lacks. That covers named packages and dependencies, and a wrong-size file, which apt deletes and queues again (acquire-item.cc pkgAcqArchive::QueueNext). Only those files are fetched; no index is fetched on a hit. If the install from the set still fails, the step falls back once to a fresh fetch with a ::warning:: naming BROWSER_CACHE_VERSION, and it is red only when that also fails. (2) SEEDING. On a push to main whose commit is already verified, the browser jobs are no longer skipped. Their `if:` is now `!cancelled()`, they call the action with seed=(verified output non-empty), and their slice step carries `if: needs.verified.outputs.run == ''`. In seed mode the action installs nothing when both entries exist, and otherwise installs and saves under main's scope. No new job, no dispatch input, no --exempt-job change. (3) tools/gate-parity.py: job_slices now reads the `if:` of the step carrying a verify.sh call, the same way it reads a job's (`_step_runs`, `_call_tier`). New cases: sv21 (allow: a step guarded by verified's output), sv22 (an unprovable step condition is a finding and its slices are not counted as run), sv23 (a release-only step makes its slices release-only). The docstring and comment lines saying every CI job is setup plus one verify.sh call now say every job that runs a gate. (4) Bounds, by the file's rule, from the longest finished run after the change: longest browser-panel 7m46s and browser-report 13m35s (both run 44385960921). The report's bound moves 26 to 28 (2x 13m35s = 27m10s). The panel's moves 16 to 18, inside its 15m32s to 23m18s range, to hold its slowest measured miss: 14m49s, run 42283005055. (5) CONTRIBUTING.md :180-185 and :210-224 describe the shape: verified is the one job running no slice, and on a verified push the browser jobs seed without their slice. THREE DEFECTS THE FIRST PROBE FOUND, and their fixes. (a) The install failed on every runner with `mkdir: cannot create directory .../lists/partial: Permission denied`, because GNU `cp -a src/. dst/` gave dst root's owner and a runner-user mkdir followed. Fix: every write to the set goes through sudo; the index is copied with `cp -p "$sys_lists"*_*` (files only); one chown hands the set to the runner user at the end. (b) The key named the image version. The probe's jobs landed on 20261111.370.1, 20261116.376.1 and 20261111.127.1 with one package-list hash, so the seed covered only its own image. Fix: key = chromium-sysdeps-<ImageOS>-<arch>-<hash>-v<BROWSER_CACHE_VERSION>, no restore-keys. (c) jc0 went red (`verified` no longer ran alone) because the seed was a job of its own. Fix: the seeding moved into the browser jobs, as above; verified is alone again, with counts 16 per run and 17 on the release tier. STAGE-TWO PROBE (fc7abaf3, ci/P169-seed-probe2), read from the logs myself. Run 44385960921, miss: the panel job (image 20261111.127.1) logged `Fetched 13.2 MB in 14s (937 kB/s)` and `Fetched 21.1 MB in 1min 31s (232 kB/s)`, about 2m20s of install, and saved both keys. The report job fetched at 20.5 MB/s; its saves logged `Unable to reserve cache` (the panel job saved first). Run 44388480667, hit: both jobs logged `Cache restored from key` for both keys (browser ~266 MB, system packages ~63 MB). The panel job was on 20261111.370.1, not the image that saved the entry, and logged `the restored set holds every file the install needs...`. The hit step has no Get: and no Fetched line in either job (88 lines from that line to the slice, counted). Install took about 20s in the panel job and 48s in the report job; the report's 35s after the restore is local, apt `Reading package lists...` 18s plus dpkg `Reading database` about 10s. No Permission denied, ::warning:: or ::error:: in any of the four logs. Each run concluded failure on vt8 (tests/test__commit_trail.py) and on pgo7 in run 2, neither in my files. STUB HARNESS (scratchpad stubs/, not committed): 20/20 on the tree. Cases: si1 full hit; si2 miss; si3 named package missing; si4 dependency missing; si5 truncated .deb (apt's size check makes it a partial fetch, not a fallback); si6 unreadable same-size .deb (the fallback runs once and passes); si7 stale index (fallback once, passes); si8 fallback failing (red); si9 miss with the archive down; si10 ownership; old1/old2 (HEAD's step: a dependency missing means dpkg refuses after `no archive is asked`, and one package missing re-fetches the index and every file); sp1-sp6 the seed decision; sk1/sk2 the key. si10 and sk1 are red on 49a34e63's action. Mutations M1-M7 are each red in their own cases. The harness's limits: its sudo is not root, so ownership is a ledger model; it models only the GNU semantics it was given (cp -a with src/.); it cannot see the _apt sandbox user, sudo's env reset, file modes beyond the owner, dpkg locks or triggers, apt's real resolver, or the cache action itself. THE KEY TRADE: without the image version, a job on any image of the distribution restores the entry. When images differ, apt answers against the set's index: a dependency the image lacks is fetched alone. If two images need different versions of one dependency, an installed version the index satisfies costs nothing; one it cannot satisfy, or a file the archive dropped, falls back once with a warning. That fallback repeats on every run of that image until the key moves (package list or BROWSER_CACHE_VERSION), because an entry is never overwritten. The set's index ages with the entry until a key change or a week-long eviction.

tasks.title: The browser install's shell is guarded in the repository, its seed path is seen on a real runner, and a seed cannot redden a verified push
tasks.description:
The browser install now lives in one composite action (.github/actions/browser-install/action.yml) that both browser jobs call, and on a push to the default branch whose commit is already verified those jobs run it with `seed` true and skip their slice. The review of that change left three things that must not ship as they are, and two smaller ones that belong with them.

1. Nothing in the repository guards the action's shell. It was developed against a stub harness (fake sudo with an ownership ledger, fake apt, dpkg, cache directories; twenty cases, seven mutations) that was never committed, so the only check of the shell is a real CI run, and a bug on the hit path falls into the fallback and leaves the job green with one warning: the regression the change removed can come back with every gate green. Commit the harness as a check this repository runs: its cases execute the action's own `run:` blocks, read out of the committed action.yml (never a copy of the shell), against the stubs. Choose its home by this repository's rules rather than by habit: a `tests/test_<name>.py` must name a module that exists (the coverage classifier reports an orphan), tools under tools/ carry their own cases and are swept, and the gate set is what `sh tools/verify.sh --list` prints, held to the workflow by tools/gate-parity.py. It must include the case that fails when a full hit falls back (a hit that fetches is red, not a warning), the ownership case that reproduces the runner's "Permission denied" on the first version of the action, and one case per seed decision. It must run on macOS and Linux and under the sweep's isolation (scratch cwd, HOME and TMPDIR; no network; no real sudo, apt or dpkg). State in its docstring what class of runner behaviour the stubs cannot see.

2. The seed path ran on no real runner: every probe was a dispatch, where `seed` is false and the lookup steps are skipped. Before filing, hand back READY-FOR-RUN with a probe-only patch (a separate diff from the task's own, clearly marked, that hard-wires `seed` true for the two browser jobs on a dispatch) and the lines to read; the orchestrator commits the task's diff plus that patch to a probe branch and dispatches twice: the first run must look both keys up, find none, install and save; the second must find both, install nothing and save nothing. The probe-only patch is never part of the task's diff.

3. PLUGIN-BUILD-GUIDE.md says a verified push to the default branch runs only tools/ci-verified.py. That was exact before the change and is false now: say what runs (two browser jobs that look the cache up and, on a miss, install and save) and what it costs.

4. A seed must not turn a verified push red for a cache it did not need, and must not fail silently either. Today npm ci, the dry run and (on a miss) apt run before and after the seed decision, and any of them failing fails the job on the default branch. Decide and state the rule: on the seed path a failure is an annotation a reader of the run sees, the job's conclusion does not redden the run, and the slice path is untouched (a failure there is red as before). If that needs `continue-on-error`, tools/gate-parity.py does not read a step's `continue-on-error` today: extend the reader so a step that carries the slice can never be the one that is allowed to fail, with a red case and an allow case.

5. The parity reader's new step-condition cases write the `- if:`-first form; the workflow uses `- name:` first with a following `if:`. Add the pin for the form the workflow uses.

ACCEPTANCE.
1. The committed check is red on the action as it stood at the first probe (the ownership defect) and on a hit that falls back, each proven by mutation of a scratch copy of the action, restored in the same command; green on the action as it is.
2. The two probe runs show the seed path's two branches on a real runner, and the outcome quotes the lines.
3. `python3 tools/gate-parity.py` and the sweep over the tools this task touches are green; `sh tools/verify.sh --list` shows the new check in a slice a per-run CI job runs, and the job's bound still has its `longest` basis.
4. On a dispatch and on a pull request the browser slices run exactly as before (the reviewer checked this for the current tree; say what in your diff could change it and why it does not).
5. The guide's sentence is exact.

tasks.title: A shard has one lock every writer takes and reads behind: the run record, the pointer and reconcile go through one helper, and a repeated verdict's record says where its steps came from
tasks.description:
The run record (`lastRun` in a task's or phase's shard, with `testEvidence` derived from it) is written by the gate under the phase lock. Its review showed that this is not the lock that serialises writers of a shard: every audit-task.py verb writes the shard under the `index` lock, and the phase lock is held only by `start`'s claim and the drive's phase run. A probe held the index lock as a verb does; the record was written after 0.02 s without waiting, and the verb's later write from its earlier read left neither `lastRun` nor `testEvidence`; in the other order the verb's write is lost. The case meant to hold this (lr4) passes because its stand-in verb takes the phase lock, which no real verb does, and lr5 asserts what the test's own read-modify-write does. CHANGELOG.md, manifest-conventions.md and PLUGIN-BUILD-GUIDE.md state "neither write loses the other's key", which is false today. Everything later in this phase reads the record, so this is fixed before any reader moves.

THE INVARIANT, to hold by mechanism and not by a list of call sites: a shard has one lock that every writer of it takes, and every writer reads the shard AFTER taking it. Find which lock that is by reading what the verbs do (`_under_lock`, `acquire_index_lock`), not by what the record's first design said, and make the record's write, the pointer's write (`write_pointer` still reads the shard before it takes its lock) and reconcile obey it through ONE helper that takes the lock, reads, lets the caller change the node, and saves; no function in _evidence_io.py saves a shard outside that helper. Whether the phase lock is still taken as well is yours to decide and to state with its reason and with the one fixed order in which two locks are taken (a second order anywhere is a deadlock); say what a gate launched by the drive, which runs while the drive's own phase run holds the phase lock, does under your rule. The bounded wait stays: a live holder is waited for up to the bound, and a record that still cannot be written exits 3 as now.

Then the rest of the review:
1. A repeated verdict's record. When the gate repeats an earlier run's verdict instead of measuring, the record's steps are copied from the ledger row of the source run; with no such row the record is `steps: []` under `verdictSource: reused` with nothing saying the steps are missing, and no case covers the arm at all (replacing the copy with an empty list left both suites green, because every record case runs with --no-reuse). A later task of this phase stops writing ledger rows, so the ledger cannot be the source. The run being repeated is, by the reuse rule, the subject's newest run, which is the record this write replaces: take the steps from the record being replaced when it is that run, from the ledger row otherwise, and when neither holds them say so in the record in a field a reader cannot mistake for an empty run. Settle with the schema what `startedAt` and `durationMs` mean on a repeated run (the schema says `startedAt` is absent there; the code keeps the read-back's own) and make code, schema and documents say one thing. Cases: the repeated arm with the source in the replaced record, with the source only in the ledger, and with neither.
2. Two writers of one key. When a ledger row is stamped after the record (a record write that was refused), reconcile moves only the pointer, so `testEvidence` and `lastRun` name different runs, against "the two always name one run" in manifest-conventions.md and COMPATIBILITY.md's sentence about the values `testEvidence` caches. Decide which is true: reconcile rewrites the record from the row it trusts, or the documents say when the two may differ and what a reader does then. One of them changes.
3. Text: the `--record` help and the comment beside the unrecorded exit say a green run; a red run exits 3 as well. The refusal printed for a dead lock holder reads "...use audit-lock --takeover, then nothing was written to the plan" and names no repair in an order a reader can follow: say what happened, then what to run.

tasks.title: The record is sufficient for every reader of the one seam: the drive finds its run after a replacement, readers read the plan they were handed, the importer takes a run held only as a record, and an unreadable shard is said as that
tasks.description:
Readers of a test-gate run now go through one seam (`_evidence_io.read_rows`) that finds a run in the plan's record as well as in the ledger. An independent review of that change found no case where a record-only run makes the commit binding accept what the ledger would have refused, and four things that are wrong or will be the moment ledger rows stop being written, which a later task of this phase does. They are fixed here, before that task.

1. The drive loses the run it launched. The launch token is only on the record; the ledger row never carries it and the union adds it to a row only while the record still holds that same run. When another run of the same subject is recorded after the launched one, or the launched run's record write was refused, the drive answers wait-gate with "no gate row ... since" for good, though the ledger holds the row. Put the token on the ledger row too, and for the time when no row is written: when the subject's newest run is later than the launch and carries another token, the drive says the launched run was replaced, by which run, and what to do, instead of waiting. Cases for both orders (the existing case covers only the foreign run landing first).

2. The record is not yet sufficient for the seam's readers. A run held only as a record gives `followersOwed`, `gateReach` and its not-asked twin, `observations`, `treeMutated` and `coverage` as None or empty with nothing saying so: the drive decides a red that owes regenerated followers as a plain red, a repeated verdict prints that its source recorded no reach reading, the panel and the report say no comparison was made. The record's keys are a hand list beside the readers. Make sufficiency a mechanism: the record carries what the seam's readers read, and a case fails when a reader of the seam takes a row key the record does not carry (derive the readers' keys by reading the code that consumes the seam, or hold an explicit table that a case compares with a real row written by the gate; say which and why). Mind the record's size bound: say what each added field costs on this repository's own task gate, and what is cut first when a run is over the bound.

3. Callers read the wrong plan. `run-test-gate.py` (several call sites), `audit-task.py`'s `_ledger_run` and `_runs_under`, and the importer's `held_runs` call the seam with no plan path, so the records read are those of the plan the project's config names while the record is written to the plan the command was handed; in a project holding more than one plan (this repository's examples), reuse and a repeat's source are looked up in a foreign plan whose task ids collide. Make the plan a REQUIRED argument of the seam, so a caller that forgets it is an error, and hand every caller the plan it was handed. A case with two plans in one project whose task ids collide: a run recorded for one is not reused for, bound to, or found from the other.

4. The importer refuses too much. It refuses a whole ledger file when any of its runs is held as a record, which is the ordinary state of a project whose plan travels with git and whose evidence files do not: the run recorded on another machine arrives in the committed shard first, and that machine's ledger file can then never be imported. Only a run held as a ledger ROW is a duplicate; a run held only as a record is imported and the union's rule decides which copy a reader sees. Rewrite the two cases the earlier change added (they pin the refusal) and say in COMPATIBILITY.md or the CHANGELOG, whichever states the importer's behaviour, what it does.

5. Messages and unreadable shards. `--base-of`, the drive's `ledger_row`, the binding and the panel's dangling sentence (plugins/audit/scripts/ui/panel/overview.js) name the ledger alone or print a zero nobody counted; a shard that will not read is skipped silently by close-phase's `tip_bodies` and `branch_records` and ignored by the importer, and three functions walk a plan's shards with three error rules (`plan_bodies`, `subject_records`, `tip_bodies`). One walker, one rule for a shard that will not read (it is reported with its file, and a reader that cannot tell "no run" from "could not read" says could not read), and each message names both places it looked. For the panel's sentence read the `refactoring-the-assembled-ui` skill and run `python3 tools/count-ui-pins.py` BEFORE editing; the change there is the sentence and what it reads, nothing else; you cannot run the browser gates, so say which pins and which non-browser suites cover it.

ACCEPTANCE.
1. Each of points 1 to 4 has a case red at HEAD and green after; the mutations that prove them are run in a scratch copy outside every checkout, restored in the same command, __pycache__ purged, each confirmed landed.
2. With a fixture plan whose ledger directory is REMOVED after the runs are recorded, every reader of the seam answers as it does with the ledger present, or says what it could not read: the commit binding (accept and refuse), the gate's reuse, the drive's read-back and its followers, `--failing-from`, `couple --basis-run`, close-phase, status, the report's and the panel's evidence facts. One case per reader, or one table-driven case that names each.
3. The previous release's plan (no record anywhere; examples/acme-store as committed) gives byte-identical status, `--gate` and report output before and after, as the earlier change showed for itself.
4. `python3 tools/check-rendered-artifacts.py --before-commit` and `python3 tools/check-example-ledgers.py` exit 0; a committed page your change makes stale is handed back BEFORE filing.
5. The record's bytes on this repository's own widest task gate, before and after, measured twice.

DEPENDANTS to answer for by name: the commit verb and `_verdict_binding`; the gate's reuse and `--base-of`; the drive (read-back, followers, timing queue, wave members' trees: which plan does a member's gate read and write?); close-phase and integrate; `audit-task.py` `--failing-from`, `couple`, group sign-off; the importer and docs/examples' CI pipelines that call it; status, the report and the panel's evidence view; the doctor's evidence and trail checks; the demo generator's schema exemptions and the schema's `lastRun` description (a field added to the record is described there); reconcile.

If a file you need is outside your list, STOP BEFORE FILING and hand back the exact change: a return is filed once per start.
